html:
SMTO-GWT-0077 — SMTO can't tell whether the GPU change happened

GUID: 94898088-a9a7-592e-84b5-be97a90159b7
Slug: gpu-operation-outcome-unknown
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO sent the change to the graphics card but couldn't confirm the result. It may have happened fully, partly or not at all, and SMTO may keep this GPU marked as busy until it is checked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to show the current details for this GPU, without asking for any change. For power limit, persistence mode and compute mode, the details show whether the new value is in place.
  2. If the details already show the value you wanted, don't ask for the change again. Sending it twice could disturb a card that is already set the way you wanted.
  3. If the details still show the old value or won't load, or you changed clock speeds or reset the GPU, send the error details to the person who manages that computer. SMTO keeps this GPU marked busy until someone checks it, and clock or reset results can't be confirmed from a reading.

What success looks like

  • The GPU details show the setting you wanted, or the person who manages the computer has confirmed the card's state.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU; they include the GPU's ID and what was requested. Don't reset the GPU or repeat the change to find out what happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The GPU configuration outcome is unknown: the receipt was lost, exact-UUID readback after the change failed or did not match, a clock or reset acknowledgment was lost, or the nvidia-smi process may still be active.

What this means

  • A configuration attempt lost its receipt, could not establish matching post-change UUID state, failed readback verification or retained a possibly active provider process. A lost clock or reset acknowledgment cannot be settled by ordinary instantaneous telemetry alone. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A configuration attempt lost its receipt, could not establish matching post-change UUID state, failed readback verification or retained a possibly active provider process. A lost clock or reset acknowledgment cannot be settled by ordinary instantaneous telemetry alone.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact UUID, before/after facts, requested setting, provider acknowledgment and owning job; respect unobservable clock constraints.

How to fix it

  • Read gpu.device for the exact UUID in the error details and compare it with requested/before/after; inspect the Gateway job named gpu_ plus the execution ID, whose unknown state keeps the GPU resource claim and blocks Local AI startup until reconciled. Never replay the mutation or reset; clock locks and resets cannot be verified from instantaneous telemetry and need operator confirmation.
  • Read the exact UUID state and reconcile existing resource ownership. Never blindly replay a mutation or reset.

Retry and execution caution

  • For a mutation, inspect the exact UUID and resolve any active execution or uncertain effect before issuing a new operation. Never replay a reset or an unobservable clock change to infer its result.

How to verify the fix

  • The original change and resource ownership are reconciled with suitable evidence before another mutation or reset.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
